The alpha-beta microstructure delivers 45% higher specific strength than 4140 chromoly steel, translating directly to gram-level weight savings where it matters. Its high-cycle fatigue endurance limit (>500 MPa @10^7 cycles) matches the pedaling load spectrum of Thermal barrier piston core insert for disc caliper. This rationale is driven by thermal barrier piston core insert for disc caliper and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for brake caliper hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g at 200W fiber laser
Go/No-Go ring gauging at 200W fiber laser
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for thermal barrier piston application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for thermal barrier piston performance

faq.q: How much weight savings does Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert offer versus steel or aluminum?
faq.a: Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert fabricated from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V provides a 40-45% weight reduction versus 4130 chromoly steel (4.43 vs 7.85 g/cm³) at the same strength. Compared to 6061-T6 aluminum, titanium's 3× higher yield strength (830 vs 275 MPa) allows 50-60% thinner walls, resulting in a net weight comparable to aluminum with 4× better fatigue life — critical for thermal barrier piston.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert?
